But when a property is passed down without a clear legal title, heirs may face legal and financial challenges that put their family home, and the wealth tied to it, at risk.
In New York City alone, between $400 million and $4 billion in family wealth may be vulnerable each year because of tangled titles, according to new research from the Center for NYC Neighborhoods supported by the Wells Fargo Foundation.
Since 2022, the Wells Fargo Foundation has supported efforts to help families address tangled titles through funding for more than 20 organizations nationwide. This includes a new grant to the Center for NYC Neighborhoods that will help launch a first-of-its-kind solution.
To learn more, visit the Center for NYC Neighborhoods’ new Heirs’ Property Protection Program.

If your parent or grandparent passes away, the last thing you should have to worry about is losing the family home or the wealth it represents.
But when a property is inherited without a clear legal title, heirs can face legal and financial challenges that make it harder to access financial services, qualify for assistance programs, or protect the property from scams.
In New York City alone, more than $400 million — and potentially up to $4 billion — in family wealth may be vulnerable each year because of tangled titles, according to new research from the Center for NYC Neighborhoods supported by the Wells Fargo Foundation.
Since 2022, the Wells Fargo Foundation has supported efforts to help families address tangled titles through funding for more than 20 organizations nationwide. This includes a new grant to the Center for NYC Neighborhoods that will help launch a first-of-its-kind solution.
Learn more about protecting your property and family wealth through the https://cnycn.org/research-and-stories/heirs-property-protection-program

A new Wells Fargo HOPE Inside center in Baltimore offers free one-on-one financial coaching to help you make progress with your debt, savings, or credit score.
Operation HOPE, Inc. coach Mike Horton helps clients form healthy financial habits that can help them through money struggles and reach their financial goals.
Watch: Meet Mike and learn about the impact of the HOPE Inside program.
Our New Baltimore Hope Inside Center

Free, one-on-one financial coaching is available in Baltimore, no matter where you bank.
At the new Wells Fargo HOPE Inside center in Baltimore, @operationhopehq Coach Mike Horton often helps clients who are spread thin financially and unsure how to move forward, offering them a plan without judgment.
“The power transfers from ‘Coach Mike knows everything’ to ‘I can do this,’” he said.
Swipe to see images from the recent launch of our Baltimore HOPE Inside center.
Operation HOPE and Wells Fargo Expand Free Financial Coaching to Baltimore

Here to answer your credit, debt management, savings, and other personal finance questions is Coach Mike Horton. From his time as a high school math teacher to his decades coaching basketball, Coach Mike has a long history of helping others reach their goals.
“Most of [my clients] didn’t learn [how to manage money] at home,” he said. “They didn’t learn it in school, and neither did I. Our conversations often start like, ‘I messed up’ or ‘I fell into a trap and now I’m stuck. How do I get out?’ It’s not their fault. They didn’t know.”
With rising costs, many who walk into HOPE Inside centers find their finances spread thin. Instead of judgment, Coach Mike offers clients accountability to help them grow in person or virtually. A little progress goes a long way to build momentum toward big changes.
“[My clients say], ‘My [credit] score went up five, 10 points, or I was able to eliminate one bill, get rid of one late payment, get rid of one collection account. Then the belief really, really kicks in. The power transfers from, ‘Coach Mike knows everything,’ to, ‘I can do this.’”
More than 25,000 people have received one-on-one financial coaching through Wells Fargo HOPE Inside centers, whether they bank with us or not. We plan to reach even more people as the number of Wells Fargo HOPE Inside centers around the country hits 50, serving more than 200 branches by the end of the year.

Like her customers, Maria knows what it’s like to work toward financial goals while navigating life’s challenges. Two years after beginning work at Wells Fargo and taking her own advice, Maria was debt free. That experience became the foundation for how she interacts with customers who enter Wells Fargo branches.
Maria sends personal greeting cards when customers have a new baby, calls on their birthdays, and asks about life changes. Because just like people and families, financial needs also evolve.
That consistency has helped her build lasting customer relationships and a strong referral network. But the moments that mean the most to her are the ones she calls “real life” in action.
When she recently helped a customer who just lost her husband, Maria drew on her own experience of losing her father when she was just 15 years old.
“That’s why I’m so passionate about connecting with people,” she said. “I want to make sure that I’m there for them.”
We celebrate employees like Maria who bring genuine care to every customer interaction and show how trust is built through real human connection. Watch Maria’s story: https://on.wf.com/6189BE7ibB
